Jordan / Sam / Laura —

Thanks for the loop. I reviewed Vitality's redline and the procurement ask. Below are our comments and a proposed clean sentence we can insert into the Limitation of Liability section. TL;DR: Redwood is willing to accept a narrowly-drawn carve-out for death/bodily injury and physical damage to tangible property, but only to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and subject to our insurance limits. We will not agree to an unlimited carve-out for ordinary SaaS operational losses or regulatory fines.

Key points:
- Our standard liability cap remains: the greater of twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form or USD 1,000,000.
- We already exclude certain liabilities (breach of confidentiality, IP indemnities, willful misconduct) from the cap; adding a limited carve-out for physical injury is acceptable if tightly drafted.
- We prefer the carve-out to read as a single, narrow sentence (below).
- We will require customary notice/cooperation provisions and confirmation of applicable insurance (commercial general liability) in the Order Form.

Proposed language to add (suggested placement after Section X.X Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither party's liability for death, bodily injury, or physical damage to tangible property resulting from such party's gross negligence or willful misconduct shall be subject to the liability cap set forth in this Agreement; provided, however, that such liability shall otherwise be subject to applicable law and any limits required by the party's commercially reasonable insurance coverages."

Rationale: the phrase "resulting from such party's gross negligence or willful misconduct" narrows the carve-out to serious misconduct and avoids opening the door to routine SaaS incidents being treated as uncapped. The insurance qualification protects Redwood against open-ended, extraordinary claims.

If Vitality's counsel would prefer different placement or minor edits, happy to iterate. I've attached a short markup with inline notes (Redwood_MSA_markup_legal_comments.pdf).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
